Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Adult male (53 y) with 1-week painless swelling over left olecranon, mild warmth, preserved function. Most consistent with aseptic olecranon bursitis; septic bursitis and gout less likely but require exclusion. No red-flag features of septic arthritis currently.

Plan:
• Start NSAID—Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (dose/route/frequency per transcript).  
• Arrange blood tests: FBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatologic antibodies, serum urate; forms mailed to patient.  
• Follow-up (video or in-person) ~6 days after testing to review results and assess elbow.  
• Safety-net advice: seek urgent review if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or systemic symptoms develop.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis – High likelihood: classic presentation with painless, mildly warm swelling and full ROM, no systemic illness.  
2. Septic olecranon bursitis – Moderate likelihood: warmth and tenderness warrant exclusion; blood tests and clinical follow-up planned.  
3. Gouty olecranon bursitis – Low-moderate likelihood: age/sex risk; test serum urate; no prior gout history.
